newsitem.title: UK: Britain targets shrub-eating Galapagos goats.
newsitem.headline: Britain targets shrub-eating Galapagos goats.

text.p: Britain is stepping into an evolutionary battle in Ecuador's Galapagos Islands by helping to pay for the eradication of wild goats threatening the survival of the giant tortoise population.

Study of the tortoises and other wildlife in the Galapagos inspired British naturalist Charles Darwin to write The Origin of Species, which sought to explain how, by natural selection, certain species survive by adapting to their environment.
Now the tortoises are to get a hand in their struggle to adapt from a government renowned for its hostility to keeping dying businesses alive.

Foreign Office minister Liam Fox said Britain had donated 500 pounds ($790) to buy equipment for a programme to eliminate the estimated 100,000 feral goats that are destroying plants on which the tortoises feed.
Fox told parliament that the Foreign Office had also earmarked 25,000 pounds ($39,450) to establish a base station for the scheme and to protect threatened plant species.
Earlier this year Britain's ambassador to Quito visited the islands to see for himself the havoc caused by the munching goats.
